question: Will U.S. grocery inflation for December 2026 be above 2.5%?

profile.label: Adults 25+ with a bachelor's degree or higher

questions.text: Will grocery prices in the US be more than 2.5% higher in December 2026 than in December 2025, as measured by the government's CPI Food at home index?
How have you changed your grocery shopping in the last year to save money?

answers.option: I use more coupons, sales and loyalty apps
I switched to cheaper store brands
I buy fewer groceries or smaller portions
I switched to a cheaper store

behaviorSummary: 42% use more coupons, sales and loyalty apps. 38% have traded down (23% to store brands, 15% to a cheaper store). 16% buy fewer groceries or smaller portions, and 4% have changed nothing.

quotes.text: Prices have stayed sticky enough that I expect food-at-home inflation to remain above 2.5%, so I've leaned more on sales, coupons, and price comparisons to keep our grocery budget in check.
Food-at-home inflation has stayed sticky, and given my own experience and the broader price trends I follow, I expect it's more likely than not to be above 2.5% over that stretch.
Food costs in New York are high enough that I pay close attention to sales, compare stores, and trim delivery fees, so I'd expect prices to keep rising faster than 2.5%.
I think food-at-home inflation will stay around or below 2.5% by late 2026, and when I do save money it's mostly by using sales and seasonal substitutions rather than making broad cutbacks.
Prices might stay around flat or move a little, but I don't see them being more than 2.5% higher once you factor in store sales and where I shop.

knownAnswerCheck.question: Were grocery prices in the US more than 2.5% higher in September 2026 than in September 2025, as measured by the government's CPI Food at home index?
knownAnswerCheck.fact: The Bureau of Labor Statistics CPI Food at home index (not seasonally adjusted) was 321.758 in September 2026 and 316.042 in September 2025, a rise of 1.8%, which is not more than 2.5%.
knownAnswerCheck.sourceName: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, CPI-U Food at home, not seasonally adjusted (series CUUR0000SAF11)
